Empirical Research Plan  
“How do effective schools impact student achievement in New York City?”

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
Strategy: Lottery-based Instrumental Variables (two–stage least squares, 2SLS).

Rationale  
• Oversubscribed NYC schools allocate seats by random lottery ⇒ assignment offer is as-good-as-random.  
• Many applicants who win do not ultimately enroll (and some losers enroll via wait-list), so we treat “offer” as an instrument (Z) for “actually attends an effective school” (D).  
• Y = student test score; estimate TOT (treatment-on-the-treated) = causal effect of attending an effective school.  
• Design delivers both an ITT (reduced form) and TOT (IV).

Alternative designs (DID, RDD) are unnecessary because the lottery already provides experimental variation.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable (D)  
  D_i = 1 if student i actually enrolls in an “effective” school (top-quartile value-added or DOE quality tier) in grade g during year t.

Instrument (Z)  
  Z_i = 1 if student i receives a lottery offer from at least one effective school applied to.

Control group  
  Z_i = 0 lottery losers who instead enroll in a non-effective school.

Treatment timing  
  Event date = first admission lottery of middle-/high-school choice round (spring of grade-5 or grade-8). We measure outcomes 1–3 years after matriculation.

(No running variable or cutoff; not RDD.)

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Random assignment (Independence)  
Lottery offers are independent of potential outcomes and covariates. Highly plausible; we will verify balance on baseline characteristics.

A2. Monotonicity (no “defiers”)  
Receiving an offer weakly increases probability of attending the offered school. Plausible: students cannot be forced out of an effective school by winning.

A3. First-stage relevance  
Lottery offer strongly predicts enrollment; check F-stat > 10.

A4. Exclusion restriction  
Lottery offer affects test scores only through actual attendance at the effective school, not via other channels (e.g., parental motivation triggered by the offer). Reasonable but must be argued and tested via balance and heterogeneous-response checks.

A5. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA)  
One student’s offer does not change another’s outcome except through peer composition already embodied in D. In large NYC system, spillovers across different schools/cohorts are limited but we will discuss.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Non-random take-up / non-compliance  
• Addressed by IV.  
• Report both ITT and TOT; show robust first stage.

T2. Differential attrition / missing test scores  
• Compare attrition rates across Z.  
• Use administrative data with near-universal coverage; run Lee bounds if small attrition exists.

T3. Multiple-offer applicants & rank-ordering  
• Include applicant fixed effects and instrument with the first effective-school offer.  
• Alternatively, restrict sample to students who listed only one effective school.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# -------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# -------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast felm/iv with clustering
library(modelsummary)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load & merge data
# -------------------------------------------------
# Assume: students.csv (student-year panel), lotteries.csv (lottery outcomes), schools.csv (school attributes)
stu  <- fread("students.csv")      # id, year, grade, demographic vars, baseline test
lot  <- fread("lotteries.csv")     # id, lot_year, offer_effective (0/1)
sch  <- fread("schools.csv")       # dbn, year, effective (0/1)

# Merge
dat <- merge(stu, lot, by = "id", all.x = TRUE)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 2. Variable construction
# -------------------------------------------------
dat[, treat   := as.integer(attends_effective == 1)]      # D
dat[, offer   := as.integer(offer_effective == 1)]        # Z
dat[, post_ts := as.numeric(test_score_std)]              # outcome standardized citywide

# Baseline covariates
covars <- c("female", "black", "hispanic", "ell", "frpl", "baseline_score_std")

# -------------------------------------------------
# 3. Balance check (pre-treatment covariates on Z)
# -------------------------------------------------
for (v in covars) {
  print(feols(as.formula(paste(v, "~ offer")), data = dat, cluster = "lot_year"))
}

# -------------------------------------------------
# 4. First stage & ITT
# -------------------------------------------------
fs  <- feols(treat ~ offer | 0 | 0 | lot_year, data = dat)
rf  <- feols(post_ts ~ offer  | 0 | 0 | lot_year, data = dat)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 5. 2SLS main specification with covariates + cohort × borough FE
# -------------------------------------------------
iv_spec <- feols(
  post_ts ~ 1 + covars |                                  # endogenous equation
  treat |                                                  # endogenous regressor list
  0 |                                                      # instruments
  lot_year + borough |                                    # fixed effects
  treat ~ offer,                                           # instrument
  data = dat, cluster = "school_id")

etable(fs, rf, iv_spec, tex = FALSE)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 6. Robustness: add baseline score × grade FE
# -------------------------------------------------
iv_rb <- update(iv_spec, . ~ . + factor(grade)*baseline_score_std)
etable(iv_spec, iv_rb)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 7. Save results
modelsummary(list(Main = iv_spec, Robust = iv_rb),
             output = "results.html")
```

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────
The prior literature on charter lotteries and NYC selective schools finds gains of roughly 0.05–0.15 standard deviations per year in math and somewhat smaller in ELA. I expect positive effects around 0.10 σ for math after two years, translating to ≈ 4 percentile points.

Key factors likely mediating these gains: longer school day/year, frequent teacher feedback, high expectations, and tutoring structures.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (IV design)
────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Random assignment/balance of Z    1  
C2: Strong first stage (F > 10)      1  
C3: Exclusion restriction credible    0.5  
C4: Monotonicity (no defiers)       1  
C5: No differential attrition / SUTVA   0.5  
Total (out of 5) = 4.0

────────────────────────────────────────
End of Plan
